questions.q: What makes something a fixed asset?
options: The company buys it to use, not to sell, and uses it for more than a year
It is bought from a foreign supplier
It is paid for in cash
questions.reason: Fixed assets such as office fit-outs, buildings and servers are used in the business for more than one year. The 40 laptops in Lesson 2 were expensed because they are under the small-asset limit.

questions.q: Why is the claims centre fit-out not booked as a DKK 600,000 expense in January?
options: Its cost is spread over its useful life through depreciation, because it is used for ten years
Expenses can only be posted in December
Because Kontorbyg A/S has not been paid
questions.reason: Depreciation spreads the cost over the years the asset is used, so January does not look terrible and the later years too good.

questions.q: With straight-line depreciation over 10 years, how much is the fit-out depreciated each month?
questions.reason: DKK 600,000 ÷ 10 years = DKK 60,000 a year, and 60,000 ÷ 12 = DKK 5,000 a month.

questions.q: What is the fit-out's book value after the March 2026 depreciation run?
questions.reason: Three months of DKK 5,000 is 15,000 accumulated depreciation, and 600,000 − 15,000 = 585,000.

questions.q: Why is the fit-out capitalised at DKK 600,000 and not 480,000?
options: Insurance is VAT-exempt, so Nordica cannot deduct the 120,000 VAT and it becomes part of the asset's cost
VAT is always added to assets in Denmark
Because the contractor charged an extra fee
Because the 120,000 is depreciation paid in advance
questions.reason: Nordica charges no VAT on premiums and in general cannot deduct VAT on purchases, so 480,000 + 120,000 = 600,000 is the cost.

questions.q: What is the posting when Kontorbyg A/S's invoice for the fit-out is booked on 01.01.2026?
questions.reason: The whole invoice, including the non-deductible VAT, goes onto the asset on 211000, and the supplier is owed DKK 600,000. There is no input VAT line.

questions.q: Which transaction creates an asset master record?
questions.reason: AS01 creates the asset master record, the asset's ID card. AFAB posts depreciation, OB52 opens and closes periods and FAGLGVTR carries balances forward.

questions.q: Why does SAP keep more than one depreciation area for the same asset?
options: Tax rules differ from book rules, so each purpose gets its own values and method
To store the asset in two company codes
To post depreciation twice to the P&L
Because each cost centre needs its own area
questions.reason: Book depreciation (area 01) is for the financial statements; Danish tax rules differ, so a separate tax area holds the tax values.

questions.q: How do the asset sub-ledger and GL account 211000 relate?
options: 211000 is the reconciliation account: it holds the total of all assets, posted through the individual assets
211000 is updated once a year from the sub-ledger
Users post directly to 211000 and assets are optional
questions.reason: Like supplier and policyholder reconciliation accounts, 211000 shows the total while the sub-ledger keeps each asset. Every posting goes through an asset, so they always agree.

questions.q: What does the monthly depreciation run (AFAB) post for the fit-out?
options: Debit 481000 Depreciation (cost centre 1000) 5,000, credit 211900 Accumulated depreciation 5,000
questions.reason: The expense goes to 481000 on cost centre 1000 and the depreciation piles up on 211900. The original cost on 211000 is not touched.

questions.q: Nordica leaves Valby on 31.12.2028 and the fit-out is scrapped for nothing. What is the loss?
options: No loss, because it was depreciated
questions.reason: After 36 months the accumulated depreciation is 180,000, so the book value is 420,000. With no proceeds, the whole book value is a loss.

questions.q: What is true about an asset under construction (AuC)?
options: It collects costs while something is being built, is not depreciated, and is settled to a normal asset when ready
It is depreciated faster than normal assets
It is an expense posted straight to the P&L
It can only be used for bought-in assets
questions.reason: An AuC is not in use yet, so it is not depreciated. When ready it is settled to a final asset and depreciation starts.

questions.q: What is the unearned premium reserve (UPR)?
options: The part of premiums already received for cover that Nordica has not yet delivered
The money set aside for accidents nobody has reported
questions.reason: If a customer pays for a year, only the months already passed are earned. The rest is a liability until the cover has been given.

questions.q: At 31.03.2026, how much of Hygge Hjem's DKK 120,000 annual premium (cover from 01.03.2026) is in the UPR?
questions.reason: One month of twelve is earned (120,000 ÷ 12 = 10,000), so 11 months, DKK 110,000, are unearned.

questions.q: In March, Nordica's written premium was DKK 2,400,000 and the change in UPR was −800,000. What is the earned premium?
questions.reason: Earned premium = written premium minus the part that is not yet earned: 2,400,000 − 800,000 = 1,600,000.

questions.q: What is the difference between RBNS and IBNR?
options: RBNS claims are reported but not settled; IBNR claims have happened but are not reported yet
RBNS is for motor and IBNR is for home insurance
RBNS is paid in FS-CD and IBNR in FI-AP
There is no difference, they are two names for UPR
questions.reason: RBNS means reported but not settled (claims handlers estimate case by case). IBNR means incurred but not reported (the actuary estimates it statistically).

questions.q: What journal posts the March increase of DKK 300,000 in claims reserves?
options: Debit 405000 Change in claims reserves, credit 260000 Claims reserves
questions.reason: The cost (change in claims reserves) is debited and the liability account for the claims reserves is credited. RBNS +50,000 plus IBNR +250,000 gives 300,000.

questions.q: Who owns the IBNR number, and who posts it?
options: The actuary owns the amount; finance posts it, usually as a monthly journal from the actuarial models
Finance invents it and the actuary posts it
questions.reason: Claims and actuarial own the reserve amounts. Finance posts them, checks them against the source reports and keeps the audit trail.

questions.q: In March, claims paid were DKK 760,000 and the change in claims reserves was DKK 300,000. What are the claims incurred?
questions.reason: Claims incurred = claims paid + the change in reserves = 760,000 + 300,000 = 1,060,000.

questions.q: Why is the DKK 12,000 actuarial consultant cost accrued on 31.03?
options: The work was done in March but the invoice comes in April, so the cost must be shown in March
To move costs from March into April
Because consulting fees are a fixed asset
questions.reason: An accrual puts a cost into the period it belongs to before the invoice arrives: debit 476500 (cost centre 3000), credit 190000 Accrued expenses.

questions.q: What happens to that accrual on 01.04.2026, and how do reserves differ?
options: The accrual is reversed so it cancels with the April invoice; reserves are not reversed but updated each month
The reserve is reversed and the accrual stays forever
questions.reason: The accrual has a reversal date of 01.04, so the cost appears once. Reserves are estimates that are posted as a monthly change, not reversed.

questions.q: A EUR 10,000 reinsurance payable to Rhein Re was booked at 7.46. At month-end the rate is 7.45. What does FAGL_FCV post?
options: An unrealised gain of DKK 100, because Nordica now owes less in DKK
Nothing, because the payable is not paid
questions.reason: 10,000 × 7.46 = 74,600 and 10,000 × 7.45 = 74,500. The payable drops by DKK 100: an unrealised gain, because it isn't paid yet.

questions.q: How much insurance tax (1.1%) is collected on March written premium of DKK 2,400,000?
questions.reason: 1.1% × 2,400,000 = 26,400. It is not Nordica's money: it sits on 290100 until it is paid to Skattestyrelsen.

questions.q: Why does the insurance business not file an ordinary VAT return (momsangivelse)?
options: Insurance is VAT-exempt in Denmark; insurance tax and lønsumsafgift apply instead
Insurers are allowed to ignore taxes
Because VAT is paid only in FS-CD
questions.reason: Insurance is momsfritaget. Premiums carry insurance tax, and financial companies pay lønsumsafgift. Confirm the details with your tax team.

questions.q: Why are the FS-CD runs transferred to the GL before the reserve journals are posted?
options: Written premium and claims paid come from FS-CD, so the reserves can only be checked once they are complete
Reserves are created by FS-CD itself
So that the period can be reopened
questions.reason: The premium and claims figures that the reserves are compared with come from the FS-CD daily totals, so the transfer must be complete first.

questions.q: What does Peter do in OB52 at the end of the close?
options: Closes posting period 03.2026 and opens 04.2026 so nobody posts into March by accident
questions.reason: OB52 controls which posting periods are open. Closing March protects the numbers that have been reported.

questions.q: What is the combined ratio for March 2026 (claims incurred 1,060,000, operating expenses 350,000, earned premium 1,600,000)?
questions.reason: Combined ratio = (1,060,000 + 350,000) ÷ 1,600,000 = 88.125%, which is the loss ratio 66.25% plus the expense ratio 21.875%.

questions.q: In the March insurer's P&L, what is the technical result and the result before tax?
options: Technical result 190,000; result before tax 230,000 after 40,000 investment income
questions.reason: 1,600,000 − 1,060,000 − 350,000 = 190,000 technical result. Adding investment income of 40,000 gives 230,000.

questions.q: In the tiny March balance sheet, assets are DKK 20,342,900 and liabilities are DKK 16,112,900. What must equity be?
questions.reason: Assets = liabilities + equity, so equity = 20,342,900 − 16,112,900 = 4,230,000 (4,000,000 earlier equity plus the 230,000 March result).

questions.q: What are special periods 13 to 16 used for?
options: Year-end adjustments, such as auditor corrections, that belong to the old year but are kept apart from December
Extra months for the next year
Posting depreciation for assets under construction
questions.reason: Special periods belong to the same fiscal year, so December's own figures stay clean.

questions.q: What does the balance carry-forward (FAGLGVTR) do?
options: Moves balance sheet balances into the new year and puts the year's result into retained earnings
questions.reason: Balance sheet accounts such as the reserves carry their balances into 2027, while P&L accounts start at zero and the result goes to equity.

questions.q: Who typically does the detailed IFRS 17 and Solvency II work?
options: Specialised tools and teams in actuarial and finance, using data from the SAP ledger
The BA, by hand in the depreciation run
questions.reason: IFRS 17 measurement, Solvency II and Finanstilsynet reporting need specialised tools and teams. The SAP ledger is the source of the numbers, so the data must be right and traceable.
